title.narrative: Life Saving Emergency Food Security Assistance for Drought Affected Households in Rural Baidoa through a Cash-Plus Approach

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia is currently facing severe drought conditions linked to the poor performance of both April/June and October/December rains compounded by funding shortfalls for humanitarian assistance. According to FSNAU, 4.4 million people are projected to face high levels including ltbrgt176,490 people in IPC4 acute food insecurity in Bay between October and December due to poor rainfall, high food prices, conflict insecurity and floods. Baidoa experience an increasing influx of IDPs, putting pressure on the strained services. About 4,200 new displacements arrived in Baidoa between November and December, according to Drought Emergency Situation Report No. 2 released on 21 December.ltbrgtTAAKULO also found that 344 people in Baidoa rural villages have been displaced from their homes. At least 124 HHs (576 ind) including 55 FHHHs in the assessed villages reported livestock death in November and December and experienced critical water shortages and significant food consumption. Over 60% of the affected HHs began to reduce the number of meals, while others engaged in more negative coping, including selling assets (27%), migration (38%), and borrowing food (35%) to bridge the food consumption deficits. HHs also anticipate resorting to further coping strategies including restricting adults’ consumption and limiting portion sizes. Women, children, the elderly and persons with disabilities are at heightened risks of protection and safety risks. ltbrgtThe AFI situation is likely to worsen as the upcoming Jiilaal dry season and resource gaps FSC partners face are expected to exacerbate the drought conditions, leaving 600,000 vulnerable people in IPC phase 4 without critical assistance.ltbrgtThe project intends to ensure immediate access to food and provide emergency livelihoods support to HHs in drought hit hardest locations. The project activities include unconditional cash assistance for HHs experiencing crisis, emergency or catastrophe levels (IPC phase 3 or worse) of food insecurity Female-headed HHs, disability or elderly headed, HHs with acutely malnourished children, HHs with PLWs, marginalised and HHs with PWDs HHs and resorting to negative coping strategies to meet the increasing food needs. Emergency livelihood support will prevent further loss of livestock and promote long-term stability of the vulnerable HHs. HHs will be identified through vulnerability-based targeting.ltbrgtTarget beneficiaries of the unconditional cash assistance are 1500 HHs (10500 ind) including 2521 women, 3047 girls, 2622 boys, 2310 men and 734 PWDs. The entitlement per HH per month is US $ 55 for 3 months via mobile money transfer mechanisms to protect the dignity of the beneficiaries. This will be coupled with emergency livestock interventions including emergency water tracking and food distribution, supporting 6000 livestock species including 700 camels, 900 cattle and 4400 small ruminants. The assistance will continue for over 6 months from January 2026 and will be coordinated with other sectoral interventions such as WASH NutritionltbrgtProject activities will be implemented in a safe and dignified manner, conducting activities in the daytime in accessible and safe locations to promote participation and prevent causing unintended harm to affected communities. Community consultations will be conducted before beneficiary identification to enhance community participation and avoid tensions. Community feedback and complaints will be regularly collected through confidential and accessible CFMs including hotline toll-free number and community helpdesks managed by trained staff to incorporate into the project implementation. Clear project information such as entitlements and the CFMs for SEA will be shared with women, PWDs and minority. Women will be at least 50% of the community committee and fill at least 50% of the committee decision-making roles. They also constitute over 50% of the project target beneficiaries and women will be registered as the cash recipients for the target HHs.ltbrgtlt/pgt
